sehemu: Part III: Procedure, Powers and Privileges of Parliament
jina: Procedure for amending this Constitution and certain laws
maudhui: (1) Parliament may enact a law for altering any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the following principles: (a) a Bill for an Act to alter any provision of this Constitution, other than a provision relating to paragraph (b) of this subarticle, or any provision of any law specified in List One of the Second Schedule, shall be supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all Members of Parliament; (b) a Bill for an Act to alter any provision of this Constitution or any provision of any law relating to any matter specified in List Two of the Second Schedule at the end of this Constitution shall be passed only if it is supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all Members of Parliament from Mainland Tanzania and not less than two-thirds of all Members of Parliament from Tanzania Zanzibar. (2) For purposes of interpreting subarticle (1), alteration of a provision of this Constitution or of a law shall be understood to include amendment or modification of that provision, repeal and replacement by another provision, or extension or modification of its application.
